title: QA Metrics: What Matters, What Doesn't

scenes.say: Which QA metrics actually matter for quality—and which ones just look good on paper?

scenes.label: Leakage
scenes.sub: Defects found after release show real gaps.
scenes.say: Defect leakage means bugs found after release. Tracking this shows real gaps in your process.
Metrics like defect leakage, test coverage, and mean time to fix bugs actually reflect product quality.
But watch out for vanity metrics. Counting test cases run or lines of code tested can be misleading if they're not tied to quality.

scenes.question: Which QA metric proves effectiveness?
scenes.right: Defect leakage or mean time to fix show real impact.
scenes.say: In interviews, don't fall for the trap—number of test cases isn't proof of quality. Defect leakage or mean time to fix are much stronger answers.
